d: For nearly sixty years, Botswana was celebrated as Africa’s ultimate economic miracle. Emerging from British colonial rule in 1966 as the world’s third-poorest nation with barely twelve kilometers of paved road, it uncovered the massive Orapa diamond reserve just one year later. Instead of succumbing to the notorious "Resource Curse" that crippled so many commodity-rich nations, Botswana built an upper-middle-income economy with stellar credit ratings, high institutional trust, and a long-standing 50/50 joint venture with De Beers (Debswana).
